subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared filename decoder live, and which channel filename paths must be migrated before this issue can close?
rationale: Repository policy keeps core lean and plugin-safe, while the current implementation has separate core and Feishu parsers and the open implementation PR is partial.

options.title: Adopt media-core shared decoder
options.body: Move the decoder into packages/media-core or a narrow SDK-exposed media boundary, then migrate remote media plus Feishu metadata/fallback paths before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep Feishu-local handling
options.body: Treat the existing Feishu fixes as sufficient for now and explicitly defer the broader multi-channel shared decoder.

options.title: Wait for another channel repro
options.body: Keep the issue as design backlog until a non-Feishu channel provides concrete filename corruption evidence.

recommendation.title: Adopt media-core shared decoder
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into packages/media-core or a narrow SDK-exposed media boundary, then migrate remote media plus Feishu metadata/fallback paths before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the clearest recent merged history on the Feishu filename fix that this issue generalizes.
